_comment: The contract between ccl.py and cclink.js. Both test suites assert against this, so a regex that drifts on one side fails the other side's tests instead of silently producing links that only work in one direction. Ids are normalised to lowercase before validation, so a hand-typed uppercase id still works; lowercasing cannot introduce a shell metacharacter. `extractable` covers the lenient front door: free text pasted from a note, out of which the first UUID-shaped run is pulled and then validated normally. `rejected` is what parse() must refuse — it guards the redirect and the launcher. `extract_rejected` is the subset that has no well-formed id anywhere in it; extract() is allowed to pull an id out of surrounding junk because its output is a link, never a command.
